title: FBR Compliance Checklist for Pakistani Businesses (2026)
metaDescription: A practical FBR compliance checklist for Pakistani businesses in 2026 — STRN, IRIS registration, POS integration, tax mapping, QR validation, and monthly reconciliation.
content:
Why a checklist beats good intentions

FBR compliance in Pakistan is not one big task — it is a handful of small ones that have to stay true over time. Most businesses that get penalised did the setup correctly and then drifted: a token stopped refreshing, a new branch went unregistered, tax rates changed and the POS did not. A simple checklist, run monthly, is what keeps that drift from turning into a notice.

Use the setup items once, then treat the ongoing items as a monthly routine.

Setup checklist (do once)

  • STRN active — confirm your Sales Tax Registration Number is active on IRIS.
  • IRIS POS registration — register every terminal and obtain API credentials.
  • Compliant POS — confirm a live FBR IRIS integration, not just a claim.
  • Tax mapping — map each product to its correct rate (standard, exempt, specific).
  • Test invoices — confirm sample sales appear in your IRIS dashboard.
  • Offline queueing — verify sales during outages sync with original timestamps.

Monthly checklist (ongoing)

  1. Reconcile your POS invoice count against the IRIS dashboard — the gap is your error rate.
  2. Verify QR codes by scanning a few recent invoices on the FBR portal.
  3. Check for software updates so rule changes are applied.
  4. Review tax mapping if FBR revised any rates.
  5. Register new terminals for any counter or branch added.

The item people skip

The monthly reconciliation is the one that matters most and gets ignored most. It is the only check that surfaces silent submission failures — invoices that printed locally but never reached FBR. Skip it and you can run non-compliant for weeks without knowing.

A real example

An electronics shop in Rawalpindi passed every setup item but never reconciled. A token problem caused a month of afternoon sales to fail silently; the gap only appeared when a customer's QR would not verify. A five-minute monthly check would have caught it on day one.

Putting it to work

Print this list and run the monthly section on a fixed date. If a reconciliation reveals missing invoices, our guide to common FBR POS issues explains the causes, and if you are still registering, the IRIS registration guide walks through the setup items.

faqs.question: How often should I run this checklist?
faqs.answer: Do the setup items once, then run the ongoing items — reconciliation, software updates, tax-rate review — every month. Monthly is the cadence that catches silent failures before they become penalties.

faqs.question: What is the single most important item?
faqs.answer: The monthly reconciliation between your POS and the IRIS dashboard. It is the one check that reveals invoices that never reached FBR, which is the most common and most dangerous compliance gap.

faqs.question: Do small businesses need to follow all of this?
faqs.answer: If you are a Tier-1 retailer with an active STRN, yes — the obligations apply regardless of size. The checklist scales down easily for a single outlet.

faqs.question: What are the penalties for missing these?
faqs.answer: Non-compliance penalties start around PKR 10,000 and rise to as much as PKR 1,000,000 for repeated violations, with possible STRN suspension. Most are avoidable by working through this list.
